reviews.comment: Dr. Nan is a sweet guy, he seems harsh but its bc his culture. Many redact how he said he wants everyone to have an A and he lowers the grading cut off. Tests are super hard but FRQ (usually packback questions) + curve turned my raw scores of 60s to 90s. final is optional too. Packback adds 5 pts to grade

Professor Beiyan was an awesome professor. His exams are HARD! I would recommend studying a lot for them. Make flashcards, read over his slides, and hope that your guessing is lucky on the multiple choice. He curves 10+ points on every exam we took. He gave a ton of extra credit through his packbacks. He was very kind and a great lecturer.

Despite my attendance at SI and heavy studying, I barely got class averages. The disconnect is undeniable the final exam average was a 58%, he blamed students rather than his teaching. He lacks basic empathy. During one lecture, he actually mocked a student to their face, laughing and calling them "annoying" in front of everyone. DONT take him!!

He was rude and full of himself, often belittling students for asking questions. Even if you studied and knew every slide, exams focused on irrelevant details not emphasized in class. Test averages were often in the 40s before curves. Overall, the teaching style and testing felt unfair and poorly aligned. Do not take him if you have another option.

Dr. Nan was a nice guy overall, a little bit hard to understand. He's known to give out the hardest 351 exams. You can study as long as possible and still get a 60 on exams (he asks INSANELY specific questions that were not mentioned in lecture). Most averages were in the mid 60s. Huge curves, though, that help you out a LOT with your final grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were very hard with exam averages in the 60s WITH a curve. He is rude and condescending if you ask him questions. Definitely take a different prof if you can.

This class was very disappointing. You could study incredibly hard, but the exams had a completely different emphasis on the topics, making all your hard work go to waste. 2nd exam was the HARDEST. Averages were always failing. I liked the professor a lot; he was kind and funny, but his exams were truly frustrating—definitely not an easy A.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most of his lecture slides are mostly pictures and hard to follow, making it difficult to study for this class. You also had to pay to receive extra credit through Packback (basically pay to win lol). He curves tests but does not provide any practice exams. Sometimes, his exam questions are very nitpicky and focus on the most specific information.

Dr. Nan was a great professor. While attendance isn't mandatory, his lectures are very informative and interesting. He doesn't make practice tests or study guides for the tests, but all the information is on his slides.

If you are a pre-med looking for an A, he is the perfect guy. However, he has a ton of drawbacks and if you have not taken super hard classes before avoid him. Tests are very challenging with high curves, and he has an attitude that honestly annoyed me throughout the semester. He encourages us to ask questions, but berates us when we don't.

I really enjoyed Dr. Nan's lectures. He made microbiology interesting for me and he heavily encouraged that students ask him questions. Exams were difficult but all of the necessary information to study was on his slides and he gave a huge curve for every exam and offered extra credit opportunities. Lab also wasn't too bad which was helpful.

Attendance not mandatory. Has free response questions on exams, exam MC questions harder than average micro classes. Questions are multi-concept based and not straight forward. Very big curves ( 20 pt. Avg each exam) 
Do packbacks, (+5 pts on overall grade) 

Very generous prof despite hard exams

Dr. Nan is passionate but very blunt so it comes off as rude. Exams are somewhat hard but he curves A LOT. There's no homework and all grades comes from labs and exams. Lab is easy. Many exam FRQs comes from his Packback questions so look at them! Write down everything he says to study later bc his slides are mostly diagrams. Overall, very doable!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nan is unnecessarily rude! This class was harder than it needed to be for microbiology. Many of my classmates agreed on this. His lectures are very heavy, he does not make it clear what you need to understand. He is very rude when you ask questions. However, he does give curves on the tests!

Dr. Nan is very passionate about microbiology and truly wants the best for his students, but his lectures are a little confusing. He never makes it very clear what concepts he wants you to understand and what will be on the exams. He gives out five points of extra credit and drops a lecture exam if you do the final.

Dr. Nan ranks in the top 3 profs of my life (as a senior). His lectures are super engaging, and you'll fall in love with the material by the way he teaches it. He encourages curiosity by asking questions and answering yours. He talks right to you and the slides supplement what he says perfectly. I recommend using Anki, as there is a lot to learn.

Dr. Nan's tests are harder than other professors but he also curves a lot. He's a great teacher and wants students to succeed. Packback is extra credit added to your overall grade. The final is optional, so try to do your best on the regular exams.

Lab experiments are fun if you know what you're doing.

Not a great teacher overall, a tad difficult to understand, and write down what he says in lecture because he will say things that aren't on the slides. Whatever you do, get packback to do the bonus points because they will be needed. I'm kicking myself because I didn't get it. SI is helpful, and study the packback questions and your notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attend every lecture, and write down everything he says verbally, you can study the slides later. Most of the exams are based on the material he says verbally and when says "I will ask this on the exam." Funny sense of humor but can be kind of rude when you ask him a question at times. Stay on top of the lab, and hope your TA is a gem.
Dr. Nan is a solid choice for microbiology. Exams were difficult and based on lecture material. He posts review questions throughout the semester that show up on exams.

Dr. Nan is one of the best biology professors that I have had. He cared for his students and just wants them to do their best! Lectures are not mandatory but his exam are solely based on lecture material so I would go to them. Lab was more tedious than anything but doable! In the end I recommend this class!

Didn't start off too well because the exams were difficult, but ended up doing well at the end. Literally one of the most caring profs I've had, and he actually does care if you do well. He curves exams depending on how everyone did, and lowers grade cut-offs too. Pay attention to lectures carefully, tests are over minor details.

Wow I was absolutely mind blown about Dr. Nan. I took Micro before this and Q dropped because lab was so dumb and I disliked the subject very much. Dr. Nan however made it so personal and cared so much. He constantly gave life advice and encouragement in and out of class. I literally am going to do research because of this class. 10/10

Dr. Nan is an incredibly kind, caring, and accessible professor. As far as the lecture component goes, he was very fair with his grading and gave plenty of practice lecture review questions that ended up being similar to his exam questions. The lab isn't difficult, just time consuming. (He doesn't run the lab) Go to office hours, he's a Great prof!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is on a curve, so it is not difficult to pass. In order to make an A, you have to go to class and do well on the first writing assignment. Also, when he says to make your answers short, he means like a sentence or less.

Dr. Nan is a great professor that cares for his students. The lecture difficulty is on par with what you would expect. You will need to understand the material very well to handle the exams. His lectures are very good and he breaks it up with funny or interesting stories. Would take again.

This class is what you'd expect. The tests are difficult, but he explains things well and is very passionate about his work. As of Fall 2017 it was his 2nd semester teaching BIOL 351. The test averages were low (50s) but he curves alot (20pts). There is no homework, and he posts review questions. He is very concept heavy. Very tedious Lab.
